citation.authors: van Campen CMC, Rowe PC, Visser FC
citation.title: Two Different Hemodynamic Responses in ME/CFS Patients with Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome During Head-Up Tilt Testing

population.description: Healthy controls of the tilt study (Table 1, Group 3 Healthy Controls, n = 47: 10 male, 37 female), recruited by announcements on ME/CFS advocacy websites, clinic posters and acquaintances of the ME/CFS participants; subjects referred for cardiology analysis were not counted as controls. Age 38 (SD 14) y as printed in Table 1 (mean and SD, one-way Welch ANOVA row); BMI is printed only as median 24.2 (IQR 21.3-27.3), so bmi is null. All controls had a normal HR and BP response on the tilt (Table 1 caption): a selection on the tilt response, not on supine HR or BP. The Results text says 48 controls had complete data, while Tables 1 and 2 print n = 47; the table n is used.

protocols.name: healthy_supine_rest
protocols.description: Healthy controls, supine rest before the head-up tilt to 70 degrees; the tilt itself is not entered (no posture input). Methods: 'all participants were positioned supine for 20 min before being tilted head-up to 70 degrees', so the arm is 20 min supine (duration_min 20, minutes 0 to 19). Results: supine image acquisition 'started at 2.5 (1.2) min before onset of the tilt' and 'lasted 0.6 (0.2) min', i.e. about minutes 17.5 to 18.1 of the rest; the window 17 to 19 min covers it. The paper prints no food, fast or meal for any group, so the arm starts from typical values (norm_center) with no meal. The paper prints no clock hour for the test; start_hour 9.0 is a placeholder. The paper does not say whether the controls' supine values were recorded in this study or in the earlier healthy-control study its Methods cite for their mid-tilt images (ref 29); it states the 20 min supine for 'all participants' and that supine image acquisition did not differ between the three groups.
